headline: High: shared MCP/networked surfaces and overlapping file/write capabilities make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can use MCP, read/write its workspace, and ingest files; open-webui exposes MCP, OpenAPI tools, and persistent web-app sessions. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from B can reach A as instructions, even though no direct pairwise integration is documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF open-webui is connected to a shared MCP or tool server that nullclaw also reads from, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF either agent treats file or tool output as trusted instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer the other agent.
mitigations: Disable shared MCP/tool endpoints between the agents.
Route inter-agent content through a strict allowlist parser.
Add provenance labels to all tool and file outputs.
Use separate workspaces and separate session stores.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch API keys and files, and both have broad network egress. nullclaw explicitly reads workspace files and handles secrets; open-webui can access local/mounted files and multiple external services. A shared workspace or mounted volume would let sensitive data flow from one agent into the other and onward to third parties.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem, mounted volume, or synced workspace, sensitive files can be exposed across the pair.
IF open-webui is configured with external APIs or search tools, data read from shared files can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct volumes.
Remove secrets from any shared directory.
Disable external connectors on open-webui for shared data.
Restrict nullclaw workspace permissions to its own UID.
requires-engineering: add per-agent encryption and access controls for shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; open-webui can run browsers and subprocesses and uses persistent shared sessions. If both are pointed at the same repo, volume, or mutable resource, they can overwrite each other’s work or race on state. No locking mechanism is documented in either profile, so uncertainty escalates.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or git repository, concurrent edits can conflict.
IF either agent is allowed to mutate shared OAuth-backed or session-backed state, last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same git branch.
Serialize write operations with a lock file.
Disable one agent’s write access during the other’s run.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level coordination primitives.

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can produce tool outputs, browser findings, and workspace artifacts; open-webui is a web UI that can consume documents, notes, and model outputs. If B treats A’s output as authoritative without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions or user-visible artifacts. The pairwise interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so the higher severity is chosen.
conditions: IF open-webui renders or forwards nullclaw output without verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF either agent is used to trigger external actions based on the other’s output, the cascade can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on cross-agent output.
Add a verification step before rendering or forwarding results.
Tag outputs as untrusted until checked.
Limit downstream actions to read-only operations.
requires-engineering: implement citation and provenance checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but they differ in data handling: nullclaw explicitly handles private keys, bearer tokens, and audit logs, while open-webui handles persistent memory, usage analytics, and external connectors. The main compliance risk is policy mismatch if regulated data is routed through open-webui’s broader integrations; no direct residency or certification conflict is documented, so this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through open-webui connectors, compliance obligations may change.
IF retention or logging settings differ between the two deployments, subject-rights handling can diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of open-webui connectors.
Disable analytics on sensitive deployments.
Align retention settings before use.
Document data-flow boundaries for both agents.
requires-engineering: perform a formal residency and DPA review.
